feedback.worked_solution:
We computed the second partial derivatives in part 5. So, the second derivative of $f$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10{y}^{2}-4 & -20xy \\ -20xy & -12{y}^{2}-10{x}^{2}+20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

- Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,\pm \sqrt{5}),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,\pm \sqrt{5})=[\begin{aligned}-54 & 0 \\ 0 & -40\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we have

$$
H(0,\pm \sqrt{5})=(-54)\cdot (-40)-0\cdot 0=2\,160.
$$

- Evaluating the second derivative at $(0,0),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(0,0)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 20\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we have

$$
H(0,0)=(-4)\cdot 20-0\cdot 0=-80.
$$
